issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out at a stop, in traffic or even at highway speed. Some cars also lose power steering, lights or wipers at the same moment, or show the electronic throttle (lightning bolt) light. Restarting may take a few minutes.
issues.why: There isn't one single cause. Owners and shops point to the TIPM power module, the electronic throttle body and its sensors, and on early cars a corroded tire-pressure wiring connector (covered by a recall). Many cars show no stored codes.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Stalling while moving is a safety risk, so get it looked at soon. Make sure all recalls are done, then ask the shop to check the TIPM, throttle body and crank/cam sensors, and to note exactly when it happens.

issues.t: Power module (TIPM) failure causes no-start and random electrical faults
issues.sym: The car won't start or is hard to start, the horn or hazard lights go off by themselves while parked, or several electrical items quit at once.
issues.why: The Totally Integrated Power Module (TIPM), the under-hood fuse and relay box with its own computer, develops internal faults and stops controlling power to the starter, fuel pump, horn and lights properly.
issues.next: Have the shop confirm TIPM codes and test the relays before replacing it. A new or properly programmed remanufactured TIPM is the usual fix; parts have sometimes been on back order.

issues.t: Heater blows cold on the passenger side
issues.sym: The driver's side gets warm air but the passenger side blows cold or weak air, and the passenger side of the windshield and windows defrost poorly.
issues.why: The heater core gets partly clogged with debris and sludge in the coolant, so not enough hot coolant flows through the passenger half. Blend door actuators were blamed at first but replacing them often didn't help.
issues.next: Check the coolant level first. A flush may help for a while, but a clogged heater core usually has to be replaced. Ask the dealer about goodwill help, as some owners got part of the bill covered.

issues.t: Shifter stuck in Park
issues.sym: You can't move the shift lever out of Park even with your foot on the brake, and sometimes the key won't come out of the ignition.
issues.why: A plastic latch and spring in the shifter's park lock assembly fail, or the shift cable stretches, so the shifter stays locked. Chrysler ran a customer satisfaction campaign (K16) on this part.
issues.next: To get moving, use the small shift-lock override button under the shifter trim. Then have a dealer check whether the campaign was done and repair or replace the shifter assembly.

issues.t: Transmission stuck in one gear (limp mode)
issues.sym: The car won't shift out of first or another single gear, engine revs are held down and speed stays low, often with a check engine light and the gear display blank.
issues.why: The transmission computer puts the transmission into a protective limp mode when it sees an electrical or sensor fault, such as a code P0882 (low power to the transmission computer).
issues.next: Pull over safely and have the codes read before agreeing to a transmission rebuild; battery, wiring or module faults can cause this. Restarting may clear it briefly, but it will return until the cause is fixed.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping, harsh shifts or failure
issues.sym: Slipping between gears, delayed or rough shifts, surging, or the transmission failing completely.
issues.why: Internal wear and control problems in the automatic transmission. Shifting complaints are among the most common problems reported for the Avenger.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have the codes read. Ask about software updates first; slipping that continues usually means internal repair.

issues.t: Alternator rattles and fails
issues.sym: A rattle, hum or grinding from the front of the engine, a battery that keeps going flat, and eventually a no-start or stall.
issues.why: The alternator and its one-way pulley wear out, most often on the 2.4L four-cylinder, so the battery is no longer charged.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. If the alternator is failing, replace it before it strands you; test the battery too, as it may have been damaged by repeated draining.

issues.t: Check engine light for intake manifold runner valve (P2004)
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P2004 or P2017, stalling at low speed or at lights, and a failed emissions test.
issues.why: A valve inside the 2.4L engine's intake manifold that changes the air path sticks open. The valve is built into the manifold, so the whole manifold is replaced and the engine computer reprogrammed.
issues.next: Have the codes confirmed and ask the dealer whether a software update is part of the fix. A car that stalls is a crash risk, so get it fixed before relying on it in traffic.

issues.t: Left cylinder head failure and misfires
issues.sym: Check engine light with a misfire, a ticking sound and loss of power.
issues.why: On early 3.6L Pentastar engines the valve seats in the left cylinder head (often cylinder 2) overheat and wear. Chrysler extended the warranty on this head to 10 years/150,000 miles for many 2011-2013 cars.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether your VIN is covered by the cylinder head warranty extension before paying for repairs.

issues.t: Ticking from worn rocker arms
issues.sym: A ticking from the top of the engine, sometimes with a misfire code.
issues.why: The roller rocker arms (cam followers) on the 3.6L wear early, especially on earlier engines.
issues.next: Get it diagnosed before it causes camshaft damage. Most of the work is removing the valve covers, so replacing all of them at once is common.

issues.t: Coolant leak from water pump or thermostat housing
issues.sym: A sweet smell, puddles of coolant under the front, a low coolant warning or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The water pump, thermostat housing, hoses or radiator seams start leaking.
issues.next: Don't let it overheat. Top off with the correct coolant and have a pressure test done to find the leak.

issues.t: Brakes squeal or grind on a newer car
issues.sym: Squealing or squeaking, especially when backing up or after the car sits, sometimes grinding, even at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners and dealers point to brake dust and the pad and rotor materials. Dealers often called it normal.
issues.next: Have pad thickness and rotors checked to rule out real wear. Quality pads and resurfaced or new rotors usually quiet it.

issues.t: No start from anti-theft key system
issues.sym: The engine won't start or starts and dies right away, sometimes with the security light flashing.
issues.why: Static discharge can upset the wireless anti-theft key system, so the engine computer won't let the car start.
issues.next: Try the spare key. If it still won't start, a dealer can check the immobilizer and reprogram or replace the module.

issues.t: Airbags and seat belt pretensioners may not work (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on, or there may be no warning at all.
issues.why: The airbag control module can short circuit and turn off the front airbags, side airbags and seat belt pretensioners. Recall 16V-668 covers 2010-2014 Avengers.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. The dealer replaces the module for free.

issues.t: Active head restraints may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The front headrests may not move forward in a rear-end crash.
issues.why: A fault in the active head restraint mechanism. Recalls 13V-282 and 17V-640.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the repair is free at a dealer.

issues.t: Steering column rivet may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: No sign while driving. The steering column may not absorb impact correctly in a frontal crash.
issues.why: A rivet in the steering column may be missing or installed wrong on some 2011 cars. Recall 11V-315.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer inspects and repairs it free.

issues.t: Loss of oil pressure can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Oil pressure warning and the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: On a small number of 2013 cars, debris could cause a loss of oil pressure in the 2.4L engine. Recall 13V-552.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If the oil pressure light comes on, stop and shut the engine off. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Fuel tank valve can break, causing a leak or stall (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or leak under the car, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: A control valve in the fuel tank assembly could break on some 2013 cars. Recall 13V-043.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If you smell fuel, don't drive the car. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak onto hot engine parts (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leak, whining steering, or a burning smell from under the hood.
issues.why: The crimped end of the power steering pressure hose could separate and spray fluid onto hot engine parts, which can start a fire. Recall 10V-475.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, stop and shut off the engine. Check your VIN for this recall.

issues.t: Brake booster pushrod clip may come off (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning, but if the clip comes off the brake pedal can stop working.
issues.why: A retaining clip linking the brake pedal to the brake booster may not have been installed correctly. Recall 10V-009.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer inspects and fixes it free.

issues.t: Corroded tire-pressure wiring can cause stalling or no-start (recall)
issues.sym: No start, a dead battery, cruise control or remote start not working, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: Unused tire pressure monitor wiring connectors could corrode and short circuit. Recall 08V-152 seals the wires.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for this recall; the repair is free.

issues.t: Cooling fan connector can short and cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, or the cooling fan not working.
issues.why: Coolant could be drawn into the left radiator fan motor connector on some 2.4L cars and cause a short circuit. Recall 07V-473.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for this recall. The dealer inspects the connector, adds a wiring overlay and replaces the fan motor.

issues.t: Front door latch cable can let a door open (recall)
issues.sym: A front door that doesn't stay latched properly.
issues.why: A problem with the front door latch cable could let the door open in a crash. Recalls 07V-104 and 07V-414.
issues.next: Check your VIN for these recalls; the repair is free.
